answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock scarce stake in a shared vault before voting or claiming rewards. A Sybil attacker may mint many keys, but every key ties up capital; splitting influence across a hundred identities costs a hundred stakes. A mesa of validators can slash stake after an evidence-backed fraud challenge. This does not prove personhood, but makes fake identities costly rather than free. The timber is capital at risk for every extra vote.
